NodeAttestor join_token
Problem
A gateway often trusts a caller that holds a valid token
or sits on a trusted network. Neither proves which machine
sends the call. Zero trust removes this implicit trust.
Each session needs proof of the user and of the machine.
SPIFFE
SPIFFE stands for Secure Production Identity Framework
for Everyone. It is a standard for workload identity. A
SPIFFE ID is a URI, such as
spiffe://mcp.local/microvm/<github id>. An SVID (SPIFFE
Verifiable Identity Document) carries the ID and proves
it. It is an X.509 certificate or a JWT. Here the SVIDs
are X.509 certificates. A workload gets its SVID from the
Workload API of the local agent.
Solution
Attestation is an identity check: a machine shows proof,
and a trusted party verifies it. Node attestation applies
this to the microVM itself. The microVM proves who it is
once and receives a short-lived identity. Each workload on
it then proves itself and receives its own. The gateway
can then check the user and the workload before each
session.
SPIRE
SPIRE stands for SPIFFE Runtime Environment. It is the
software that implements SPIFFE. The SPIRE server is the
certificate authority of the trust domain. The SPIRE agent
on a node attests the node, then the workloads on it. Here
the server runs in the kind cluster and the agent runs in
the microVM.
Flow
1 spire.py: token generate -ttl 600 -spiffeID alias, bundle show
2 The server creates the alias entry, returns token and bundle
3 spire.py writes join-token (mode 600) and bundle.spiffe
4 sbx mounts ~/.sbx/spire read-only, the kit starts spire-agent
5 The agent sends the join token to port 18081, trusts the bundle
6 The server marks the token used, issues the agent and alias SVIDs
